result.consistency_note: No requirement contradiction found: AC-03 (command line, empty stdin -> four zero lines) and AC-01 (programmatic, stdin_text='' -> silent 0) are different call scopes, and AC-22's char_count 5 for '  \r\n \r\n' agrees with BC-02/BC-06; the historical 6 was already removed. One cross-source difference must be disclosed: the Verifier's bytecode_scope recorded examples/text-stats/__pycache__/text_stats.cpython-313.pyc as 14916 bytes / sha256 61a19a44... / mtime_ms 1792240028925, while my pre-run and post-run manifests record 14885 bytes / sha256 453ece51... / mtime_ms 1792244851273. That file was a stale cache written at 21:07 from an older revision of text_stats.py; my own read-only pre-check imported text_stats in-process without PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE, which regenerated the stale cache (new mtime 21:47:31) before the controlled test window. The canonical test run itself wrote nothing: the before/after manifests around it are byte-identical, and the two delivered artifacts are unchanged across the Coding report, the Verifier run and my run (sha256 17e12277... for text_stats.py and caaca9d4... for test_text_stats.py, identical in all three sources). No deliverable file was modified by me; the only file I wrote is this evidence file.
result.summary: Reviewed the delivery by reading examples/text-stats/text_stats.py, test_text_stats.py, README.md and sample_input.txt, and by executing both the canonical unittest command (exit 0, Ran 81 tests, OK — matching the Verifier's 81) and an independent script covering AC-01..AC-20 plus BC-09/BC-23/BC-24/BC-25. Every acceptance criterion AC-01..AC-25 is satisfied: the two call scopes are separated, both line counters come from one LF split, word/char tables and the five silent-vs-verbose error paths behave as specified, and the README no longer cites crlf_cr.txt or the impossible char_count 6. The only discrepancy is a stale __pycache__ .pyc regenerated by my own pre-check import, disclosed in consistency_note; the delivered .py files are byte-identical to the Verifier's artifacts. Verdict APPROVED.
